resources.string: Allow is the only action for this type.
NightJar cannot hold or block this type. Use the row of the type that it arrives as, for example Data message to a port.
NightJar cannot block or hold emergency alerts.
This message has no text. The phone only sends a confirmation to the network.
Shows on the screen. Android does not save it.
Replaces an earlier message in your messaging app.
Turns the voicemail indicator on or off.
Controls visual voicemail on your phone.
Tells you about a call that you missed.
A message from your mobile carrier.
Configures chat features on your phone.
A code that an app receives by message.
A message for an app, sent to a data port.
Tells the phone that a picture message is ready.
A push message that opens a web link.
Tries to change your network settings.
Asks your phone to contact a device management server.
Asks the phone for its location.
A push message of another type.
The network sends data to your SIM.
A broadcast message from the network.
A message for the software of the phone maker.
A message that an app added to your messages.
NightJar records all messages. NightJar blocks nothing.
NightJar records all messages. It holds or blocks the hidden message types that can be a risk. It notifies you about suspicious messages.

NightJar allows regular SMS and emergency alerts. It holds flash SMS, voicemail indicators, MMS, email and DRM notifications, and data messages to unknown ports. It blocks the other types that it can block. It notifies you about the remaining types and about unusual messages.
NightJar holds every type that it can hold, except regular SMS and emergency alerts. It blocks or notifies you about the other types.
NightJar can never block or hold emergency alerts. NightJar still records them.
A blocking hook failed to load, so NightJar cannot block messages.
The NightJar module is not active yet. Turn on NightJar in Vector or LSPosed. Then reboot the phone.
Safe mode is on, so NightJar paused blocking.
NightJar records it. Nothing else happens.
NightJar records it and notifies you, based on its severity.
NightJar holds it until you decide. No other app receives it.
NightJar blocks it before any app sees it.
If NightJar blocks this type, %1$s does not work as intended. Calls and normal messages still work.
The network tells the phone to keep the message on your SIM.
A delivery report for a message that you sent.
Asks you to call a number.
Sends data to the phone, not to the SIM.
Tries to unlock the phone from a network.
A message for a device that you connect to the phone.
A message for a fax, a pager or a different type of device.
A message that has no content.
A message that has data and no text.
A message that has compressed content.
A long message. Some parts did not arrive.
Cut address or too short. It can crash a phone.
Data for the phone, for example a ringtone or a contact card.
Asks the phone for its location through a data port.
A push message that deletes web pages from the browser cache.
Starts a sync of your contacts or calendar.
Tells the phone that new email is available.
Sends the rights for protected media files.
A push message with a contact card or a calendar entry.
A push message for a chat service.
A push message that NightJar cannot read.
A broadcast message for your SIM.
You turned off blocking. NightJar records messages but does not block or hold them. Use the Blocking switch to turn it on again.
NightJar saved the change. The phone service did not receive it. NightJar sends it again when the phone service connects.
NightJar will record messages but will not block or hold them.
Wrong message type. NightJar cannot check it.
NightJar cannot release this type later, so it cannot hold it.
NightJar can only allow this type. Select the bell to get a notification for each message.
NightJar sees only what reaches Android.
Some networks send messages that the modem of the phone answers. The modem does not tell Android, so NightJar cannot see or block these messages.
They use the internet, not SMS.
Google Messages sends RCS chats over the internet. NightJar monitors only SMS, so it does not see RCS chats.
The receiving app decides what to show.
NightJar records when Android gives a message to an app. NightJar does not record what the app does with the message after that.
NightJar records messages that arrive before you unlock the phone. Notifications cannot show the content of these messages until you unlock the phone.
The phone maker\'s service sees it first.
Some OnePlus and Oppo builds send messages through their own service first. NightJar then reports the message as handled by the phone maker.
